blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4 chart object table, `ruralz-control` StatefulSet row) and Bootstrap and enrollment (Control-mode bootstrap step 2)
blocking.issue: This regression comes from the L1-1 fix. The chart keys bootstrap on pod ordinal, not on install state. Per Control plane and GitOps, `ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store generates new CAs and leads. So if ordinal 0 ever restarts on an empty volume after install, it bootstraps a second, independent single-voter deployment with a new trust root. That happens when an operator deletes the PVC of a zonal volume stuck in a lost zone (the pod is otherwise unschedulable under `DoNotSchedule` spread), or after storage loss. Ordinals 1 and 2 still hold quorum, but the 8090 and 8091 Services now load-balance across two deployments: split brain after install. Operators and CI writing through the 8090 Service can land on the rogue leader. The old ordinal-0 voter also stays in the Raft configuration. For ordinals 1 and 2, the doc does not say that `join` runs only when the volume holds no peer certificate. Re-running `join` on every restart would need a fresh one-time token each time, and the bootstrap Job's credential is one-time. So a replaced replica can never rejoin unattended.
blocking.evidence: "Only ordinal 0 runs `ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store; ordinals 1 and 2 run `ruralz control join`, then `serve`" and "2. **First replica.** `ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store creates or loads the CAs and leads ... No other replica runs `serve` on an empty store." Control plane doc: "`ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store generates the CAs or loads supplied ones". Chart row: "`topologySpreadConstraints` on the zone label for every pod, `maxSkew: 1`, `whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule`".
blocking.fix: Key bootstrap on install state, not on ordinal. A pod runs `serve` on an empty store only on first install, for example while a chart-held bootstrap marker is absent and no peer answers on the headless 8092 Service. Otherwise any pod with an empty volume, ordinal 0 included, stays not ready until an `admin` removes its old voter and it runs `join` with a new token. State that `join` runs only when the volume holds no peer certificate. Add an Open question for replacing a replica after volume loss: (a) a chart Job that removes the stale voter and mints a new join token under a standing credential (proposed), or (b) a documented manual step. Link it to [High availability and disaster recovery](04-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery.md).

blocking.section: Sizing defaults (Node container row and first-order example) and Topology catalog (T4 HorizontalPodAutoscaler row)
blocking.issue: The L1-4 fix sized the container for idle TLS connections plus the default budgets (about 3.2 GiB). The dependency's worst case at the same default, non-configurable ceilings is about 19 GiB plus snapshots, sized for a 32 GiB Node. Each connection can hold about 592 KiB before a handler runs, and each in-flight unit about 320 KiB. The connection ceiling is fixed at 20,000 (OQ-data-plane-1 option (a) is current) and the Node gives no way to lower it. So a 4 GiB container with `GOMEMLIMIT` at about 3.6 GiB is OOM-killed by about 6,000 connections that hold large header blocks and HTTP/2 receive buffers. Because the balancer spreads the same pattern to every Node, the pods crash-loop together and the Cluster loses its capacity. The HPA connection threshold of 10,000 per Node (about 5.6 GiB of per-connection memory) scales out only after the container has already passed its memory. That is unbounded memory against the container limit, and it contradicts Performance budgets.
blocking.evidence: "Node container | 4 vCPU (target) and 4 GiB (hypothesis): Performance budgets' 2.2 GiB (target) excludes Plugins and full state tables" and "→ 4 GiB container; Performance budgets' informational run: 2.5 GiB (target)" and "`minReplicas` holds the headroom and, without an adapter, peak connections / 10,000 (target)". Performance doc: "Worst-case Node | About 19 GiB plus snapshots, fitting 32 GiB (hypothesis)". Data plane: "Per-connection memory | About 592 KiB before a handler runs (hypothesis)" and "about 19 GiB plus snapshots, fitting a 32 GiB Node (hypothesis) ..., else the connection ceiling is lowered first".
blocking.fix: In the Node container row, state that 4 GiB (hypothesis) covers idle TLS connections plus the default buffered-bytes and state-table budgets only. The default ceilings' worst case is about 19 GiB plus snapshots, sized for 32 GiB (hypothesis, Performance budgets). Give two options: (a) size Nodes for the worst case, or (b) keep 4 GiB and cap connections per Node at the L4 balancer so that connections × 592 KiB plus in-flight units × 320 KiB plus 1.24 GiB of budgets stays under `GOMEMLIMIT`, roughly 2,500 connections (hypothesis), with the HPA connection threshold at half that cap. Add an Open question asking Data plane for a configurable connection ceiling (OQ-data-plane-1 (b) or (c)). Keep OQ-deployment-topologies-8 for measured values.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4 Bootstrap Job and RBAC rows) and Open questions (OQ-deployment-topologies-11, -12)
blocking.issue: The two proposed options that make the chart's bootstrap unattended do not fit together, so the L1-1 fix cannot be built as proposed. OQ-11 (a) has the first `serve` write a one-time bootstrap credential. That credential lands inside ordinal 0's container or volume. OQ-12 (a) has the bootstrap Job read an `admin` credential from a Kubernetes Secret. Nothing moves the credential from ordinal 0 into that Secret: the RBAC row gives `ruralz-control` no right to create or update Secrets, and Helm cannot learn a value generated at runtime. Under the proposed options, ordinals 1 and 2 wait for join tokens forever.
blocking.evidence: "Bootstrap Job (proposed) | Mints their join tokens at `/api/v1/replicas` with a one-time `admin` credential from a Secret (OQ-deployment-topologies-12)"; "OQ-deployment-topologies-11 | How is the first `admin` and `security-admin` created? | (a) The first `ruralz control serve` writes a one-time bootstrap credential (proposed); (b) process configuration"; RBAC row: "`ruralz-control`: `list` and `watch` on `ruralz.io` CRDs in bound namespaces, reads of cluster-scoped `Environment` and `Cluster` CRDs, cluster-scoped CRD status updates. None reads Secrets cluster-wide".
blocking.fix: Close the path for the chart. One way: the chart generates the one-time bootstrap credential into a Secret, and ordinal 0 imports it through process configuration at its first `serve` (OQ-11 option (b) for T4). The Job reads the same Secret, and the credential is invalidated after its first use or once both joins finish. The other way: grant `ruralz-control` `create` on one named Secret in its own namespace, and add that to the RBAC row. Record which option OQ-11 proposes per topology.

non_blocking.suggestion: The body is 4,499 words under the manifest's word_count_rule, against a maximum of 4,500. The fixes above need room made by tightening prose elsewhere, for example by merging the T9 relay sentences or shortening the T10 bullets. Do not delete text that resolved L1-1 to L1-9 or earlier findings from other lenses.

`RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable` on a StatefulSet depends on the MaxUnavailableStatefulSet feature, which is not GA on every supported Kubernetes version. Without it, updates replace one pod at a time and wait for Ready, so one Control-mode pod stuck not ready stalls a 30-pod upgrade. State the minimum Kubernetes version or the fallback.
"At least three in at least two equal zones" cannot hold, because three Nodes do not split into two equal zones. Write "four in two equal zones, or three in three (target)" to match RA-1.
